config_name: XPS 14 — Core Ultra 7 358H, 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 14" QHD+ 2.8K 120Hz touch

specs.ports: 3x Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) with DP 2.1 + PD, universal audio jack
specs.keyboard_notes: Backlit keyboard, zero-lattice design, Gorilla Glass 3 palmrest

battery.notes: 70Wh. 16-core H-class CPU + higher-res touch panel costs ~1-1.5h vs the 2K LCD base per CNET line testing.

reviews.quote: It's great to see Dell bring back the XPS and do so with such style.
Matches MacBook Pro in price but not performance

praises: 16-core Ultra 7 358H + 32GB is the creator sweet spot — dell.ca owners cite smooth heavy workloads and video editing
2880x1800 120Hz touch panel fixes the base tier's soft 1200p
Still 1.38 kg despite the H-class chip — the 2026 chassis runs cool under load (owner summary: "quiet, efficient cooling")
Full Arc iGPU tier gives playable light gaming, unlike the 8-core base
32GB soldered from the factory means no early RAM regret
complaints: $3,680 approaches MacBook Pro territory where CNET says XPS 'matches in price but not performance'
Touch panel is glossy IPS — no OLED option on the 14 this year (OLED only on XPS 16)
Still no fingerprint reader, still USB-C-only ports
Dell's 'Estimated Value' anchoring ($4,679) inflates the apparent discount
Some units ship with the zero-lattice keyboard feel issues owners report across the line

design_philosophy: The performance tier of the relaunched XPS 14: Dell moves to the 16-core 358H with Arc-class iGPU and 32GB while keeping the 14.6-15.2 mm slab. It is the config for buyers who edit on the road but refuse a discrete-GPU brick.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET XPS 14 (2026) 8.1 anchor: +CPU cores and Arc iGPU → productivity +1, gaming +1 (Arc tier ~4.5 per NOTES calibration), battery −0.5 for H-series + 2.8K touch, screen_quality +1 for QHD+ 120Hz touch, thermals −0.5 for the hotter 358H.
